title: Paramedics brought Tasered man back to life
article: For 15 minutes, a Vancouver man came back to life after being fatally zapped with a Taser.
Gail Holotuk, an advanced life-support paramedic, said Roman Andreichikov was clinically dead when she treated him on May 1, 2004.
The 25-year-old gym trainer was high on crack cocaine and had been Tasered twice during a struggle with police when his heart failed.
"I was told the patient had smoked a rock of crack cocaine, went berserk, was trashing the apartment and was being subdued by the police," she told a coroner's inquest yesterday.
Andreichikov had no pulse, was not breathing and was blue in the face.
Holotuk got his heart going by injecting him with adrenaline and putting an oxygen tube down his throat.
"He was alive when we left the apartment and was still alive when we got him to the hospital," said Holotuk.
She remained in the trauma-room with the extremely fit man as he struggled for life at St. Paul's Hospital.
But she said Andreichikov had another cardiac arrest and could not be revived by the emergency team.
Paramedic Trevor Zechel was first to arrive at the apartment to help "an aggressive, suicidal male," but police told him to wait before attending the patient.
Police had called for a leg-strap and police wagon.
Zechel waited outside in the hall until a constable said "get EHS in here now."
Zechel said that when he went in Andreichikov looked dead.
Zechel cut the man's shirt off, took the Taser wires off, thumped his chest and did CPR. But he couldn't feel a pulse.
Zechel said paramedics often restrain patients in cocaine psychosis by strapping them to a stretcher, but in this case the police were there first and had taken control.
Const. Brian McKeddie said four officers were on top of a struggling Andreichikov while they waited for the leg-strap to arrive.
He and his partner were kneeling on Andreichikov's chest and another two officers were on his legs when he stopped breathing.
